newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money edges up on tax payments.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money edges up on tax payments.

text.p: Jakarta call money edged up to 12.0/13.0 percent from 10.0/11.0 percent on Tuesday morning on increased rupiah demand for weekly tax payments, dealers said.
They said slightly higher tax payments due Tuesday were behind the rise amid a neutral central bank money policy.
Longer-term rates were firming, with one- and three-month was quoted at 12.75/13.00 and 13.25/13.50 percent respectively.
One local bank dealer said Tuesday tax payments were only moderate and expected larger amounts due this Friday.
The central bank offered one-week bilateral SBIs at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.25, one-month at 10.25, three-month at 11.25, six-month at 11.5 and one-year at 12.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 9.93 percent, compared with 11.78 percent last Friday.

Bond dealers said the secondary market remained quiet, with sellers seen outnumbering buyers. They said focus was still on primary issues, with sentiment on property bonds seen slightly weak while it was positive on finance and industry issues.
Another new issue is the 600-billion rupiah five-year straight bonds by Jakarta International Hotels & Development . Traders expected its coupon to range between 15.85 and 16.25 percent per annum.
